decisions.reason: Confirmed nonfatal interface attribution error: the integration-by-parts Statement assumes DC and countable choice only, whereas the Gaussian suppliers assume AC. All three hypotheses were already explicit in this item's Statement and Given, so no inference lacked an assumption. Corrected axiom_use, A1 and F3. Checked the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck generator, vanishing Gaussian boundary terms, entropy endpoint limits, weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and integral of exp(-2t)=1/2; the proof and Statement are unchanged.

Confirmed nonfatal interface attribution error: the product-measure theorem assumes sigma-finiteness, satisfied by probability marginals; the norming-family lemma assumes HB and countable choice, with HB supplied under the explicitly assumed AC by A2. Corrected A1 and axiom_use. The jointly Gaussian finite-coordinate covariance has zero mixed blocks, so its characteristic function factors; uniqueness and generating cylinder rectangles give equality with the product law, including singular and zero-space cases. No hypothesis or Statement changed.

Confirmed nonfatal overbroad supplier restatement: log-Sobolev requires C2 g with bounded first and second derivatives, which F1 omitted. Corrected F1 to that exact domain. The actual application already uses smooth bounded f with bounded derivatives, so exp(lambda f) has both positive bounds and bounded first two derivatives. The Herbst centered-mgf inequality, Markov optimization, Gaussian smoothing of clipped Lipschitz f, integrable exponential majorants and L=0 branch are sound. Reexamined the repaired log-Sobolev supplier: only its assumption attributions changed, leaving this application valid.

Confirmed fatal logic defect in the reviewed item: a covariance kernel alone does not specify the mean, so the asserted N(0,1) marginals do not follow (m(i)=1 gives the same kernel). Specified m=0 and derived independence instead of assuming it in Given. For the assigned uniqueness objection, the GP supplier already proves finite Gaussian identification using characteristic functions and the multivariate definition constructs the independent product; the example nevertheless omitted that uniqueness interface from its direct citations. Added the existing characteristic-function lemma as F6 and explicitly identified the laws. Checked repeated-index PSD, the (1-q)^n tail limit, cylinder measurability of ell2 and the pushforward mass contradiction.

False positive: 'AC is inherited from ... suppliers' describes carrying their required hypothesis into this lemma; it does not claim that their conclusions prove AC. Both Statement and Given explicitly assume AC, and A1 invokes the choice-implication theorem under AC to obtain DC/countable choice. A2 supplies HB; the ultrafilter and Hilbert-reflexivity hypotheses are thus met. Checked integral D_h^2=exp(||h||_H^2)<=e, the common compact K giving H1 subset K-K, and weak subsequences identifying Banach limits in H1 (weak limit norm<=1 by testing against itself). The item is sound and unchanged.

repair_notes.claim: Ent_gamma(g) <= one half the Gaussian integral of |gradient g|^2/g, with positive bounded C2 g and bounded first two derivatives.
Jointly centered Gaussian Banach random elements with all mixed covariances zero are independent.
For L-Lipschitz f, the Gaussian upper deviation probability is at most exp(-r^2/(2 L^2)) for r>0; for L=0 it is zero.
The zero-mean equality-kernel cylinder process on natural indices has independent standard normals and probability zero of an ell2 coordinate sequence.
